title: [Bug] eagle: broadcast finalized verify decision across TP ranks (#31071)
body_opening:
## Motivation

Fixes #31071.

In EAGLE / spec-v2 verify (`eagle_sample` in `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py`), the **greedy** branch computed the accepted-token set from a **per-rank local `torch.argmax(next_token_logits)`** and did **not** broadcast the result across tensor-parallel ranks. Only the **sampling** branch broadcast `predict` / `accept_index` / `num_correct_drafts` from rank 0.

When per-rank `next_token_logits` differ from a non-deterministic all-reduce (e.g. AMD `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`) and a logit is **near-tied**, `argmax` picks a **different token per rank** → ranks **accept a different number of drafts** → committed `seq_lens` / batch shapes diverge

ev_microbenchmark: [body] Observed in production on **sglang v0.5.12.post1** (ROCm 7.2, MI350X/gfx950), **tp=2**, EAGLE (`--speculative-num-steps 3`, `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`), `--attention-backend triton`, `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`.
ev_end_to_end: [body] Both scheduler ranks wedge in `resolve_seq_lens_cpu → Event.synchronize`, `num_running_reqs` freezes, gen tok/s → 0, and `/health` still returns 200 until the scheduler watchdog kills the process.
ev_accuracy_eval: [body] Likely the same root cause as #24440 (EAGLE accuracy on AMD), which surfaces the divergence as wrong output rather than a hang.
ev_numerical_tests: [body] - The maintainer noted AMD GPUs were hard to rent for repro; the added CPU unit test below is the CI-runnable guard for the regression.
ev_multi_hardware: [body] AMD `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`) and a logit is **near-tied**, `argmax` picks a **different token per rank** → ranks **accept a different number of drafts** → committed `seq_lens` / batch shapes diverge → **the next TP collective deadlocks**.

title: [AMD][Perf] Fuse QK Norm + RoPE into single aiter op for Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 on HIP
body_opening:
## Motivation

In Qwen3.5's full-attention layers on HIP, the per-layer `self_attention` path runs the Q/K norm and the rotary embedding as **two separate GPU kernels** before attention:

1. `_fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_kernel` — GemmaRMSNorm of q and k (5.09 us)
2. `_triton_mrope_forward_fused` — interleaved 3-D MRoPE (5.71 us)

Together these cost **10.80 us per attention layer** and require two kernel launches. Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 uses GemmaRMSNorm Q/K-norm followed by an interleaved 3-D MRoPE with *partial* rotary (`rotary_dim=64` < `head_dim=256`, `mrope_section=[11,11,10]`, positions shaped `[3, num_tokens]`). The general-purpose `fused_qk_norm_rope_2way` aiter op cannot represent eith

title: Fix InklingDetector crashing on a streamed JSON-string tool-call payload
body_opening:
## Motivation

`InklingDetector.parse_streaming_increment` raises an unhandled exception when a tool-call payload arrives as a JSON string instead of an object. Because it escapes the public streaming entry point, it surfaces as a 500 rather than as a rejected tool call.

`partial_json_parser` defines its **own** `JSONDecodeError`, unrelated to the stdlib one, with exactly two subclasses — `MalformedJSON` and `PartialJSON`:

```python
>>> issubclass(PartialJSON, json.JSONDecodeError)   # stdlib
False
>>> issubclass(PartialJSON, MalformedJSON)
False
